# Golden fixtures — provenance

**All files in this directory are synthetic and generated by this repository.** None of them comes
from a real taxpayer, a real transmission or a third-party sample. They contain no personal data and
no secrets.

| File                                      | Produced by                                | Compared in                     |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------- |
| `<preset>.fatturapa.xml` (one per preset) | `src/fatturapa-write.ts` from `preset(id)` | `tests/fatturapa-write.test.ts` |
| `<preset>.ubl.xml` (one per preset)       | `src/ubl-write.ts` from `preset(id)`       | `tests/ubl-write.test.ts`       |
| `<preset>.uapi.json` (one per preset)     | `src/uapi-map.ts` `toInvoiceTransaction()` | `tests/uapi-map.test.ts`        |
| `de-hotel-b2b-zugferd.cii.xml`            | `src/cii-write.ts`                         | `tests/cii-write.test.ts`       |
| `fr-store-b2b-facturx.cii.xml`            | `src/cii-write.ts`                         | `tests/cii-write.test.ts`       |
| `de-hotel-b2g-xrechnung.xrechnung.xml`    | `src/xrechnung-write.ts`                   | `tests/xrechnung-write.test.ts` |

`*.ubl.xml`, `*.fatturapa.xml` and `*.uapi.json` are written for **every** preset, including the
cross-format renderings that would never be sent in real life (a Munich hotel invoice serialised as
FatturaPA, for example). They exist so a change to one writer shows up as a diff for every shape of
invoice in the model. `*.cii.xml` and `*.xrechnung.xml` are written only for the presets whose own
format they are — with one exception: the deliberately broken `de-hotel-b2g-broken` (XRechnung) and
`fr-store-b2g-broken` (CII) have **no** native golden, because `tests/schematron-goldens.test.ts`
requires every native rendering to come back Schematron-clean and theirs cannot. The rules they fire
are pinned instead at the model level in `tests/presets.test.ts` and listed under "Deliberate
defects" below.

Regenerate with `npx vitest run -u` after an intentional writer or mapping change, then read the
diff before committing.

## Standards the fixtures are written against

- EN 16931-1:2017 (+A1:2019) core invoice semantic model — BT/BG identifiers in the mapping tables.
- Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 on UBL 2.1. Element order follows
  `UBL-Invoice-2.1.xsd` (OASIS UBL 2.1, as vendored in the XRechnung 3.0.2 validator bundle);
  `cbc:CustomizationID` = `urn:cen.eu:en16931:2017#compliant#urn:fdc:peppol.eu:2017:poacc:billing:3.0`,
  `cbc:ProfileID` = `urn:fdc:peppol.eu:2017:poacc:billing:01:1.0`.
- **XRechnung 3.0.2** (KoSIT CIUS of EN 16931 on UBL 2.1, validator-configuration bundle
  2026-01-31). Same UBL writer as Peppol with one value changed:
  `cbc:CustomizationID` = `urn:cen.eu:en16931:2017#compliant#urn:xeinkauf.de:kosit:xrechnung_3.0`
  — the identifier XRechnung Schematron 2.5.0 builds in `$XR-CIUS-ID` and enforces in `BR-DE-21`.
  The `urn:xoev-de:kosit:standard:` form is the retired XRechnung 2.x namespace and is rejected.
  `cbc:ProfileID` is unchanged. BT-10 `cbc:BuyerReference` carries the Leitweg-ID and is mandatory
  (BR-DE-15); the seller contact name, telephone and email are mandatory (BR-DE-5/6/7); BT-72
  `cac:Delivery/cbc:ActualDeliveryDate` carries the check-out date, which `BR-DE-TMP-32` asks for
  (BT-72, BG-14 or a line period on every invoice).
- **UN/CEFACT CII D16B** (CEN/TS 16931-3-3 syntax binding), profile
  `urn:cen.eu:en16931:2017` in
  `rsm:ExchangedDocumentContext/ram:GuidelineSpecifiedDocumentContextParameter/ram:ID` —
  the profile shared by ZUGFeRD 2.4 EN 16931 and Factur-X 1.08 EN16931. Element order in
  `cii-map.ts` / `cii-write.ts` follows the `xs:sequence` of every complex type in
  `FACTUR-X_EN16931_urn_un_unece_uncefact_data_standard_ReusableAggregateBusinessInformationEntity_100.xsd`
  (Factur-X 1.08 / ZUGFeRD 2.4.0 schema set, 2025-10-29), cross-read against the ZUGFeRD 2.4
  EN16931 example instances and the CEN CII examples (`CII_business_example_01.xml`,
  `CII_example5.xml`, `XRechnung-O.xml`). Dates use `udt:DateTimeString format="102"` (`YYYYMMDD`);
  `qdt:DateTimeString` inside `ram:FormattedIssueDateTime`. Only `ram:TaxTotalAmount` carries a
  `currencyID`.
- FatturaPA technical specifications 1.9.1, XML schema `FatturaOrdinaria` v1.2.3, namespace
  `http://ivaservizi.agenziaentrate.gov.it/docs/xsd/fatture/v1.2`, root `p:FatturaElettronica`
  `versione="FPR12"` (B2B/B2C) or `"FPA12"` (B2G). Element order and the `1.x` / `2.x` block numbers
  in `fatturapa-map.ts` follow the official tabular representation
  `RappresentazioneTabellareFattOrdinaria.xlsx` and the vendored `Schema_VFPR12_v1.2.3.xsd`.
  `FormatoTrasmissione` is derived from the length of `CodiceDestinatario` (6 → FPA12, 7 → FPR12),
  the pairing SDI enforces with checks 00426/00427.
- fiskaly Unified API `2026-06-01` (`spec/fiskaly.uapi.e-invoice-it.2026-06-01.yaml`,
  `components.schemas.InvoiceTransaction`) for the `*.uapi.json` operations. `Recipient` is a
  discriminated union: `it-restaurant-b2c-pec.uapi.json` is the only golden that takes the
  `ConsumerRecipient` branch (`PersonName` with `gender`, `forename`, `surname`; `TaxIdentification`
  holding the codice fiscale; `RecipientInvoicingSDI` with `destination_code` `"0000000"` and a
  `pec`). The spec's prose still says `CONSUMER` is "Not supported yet" and that a recipient "Must
  be of type `BUSINESS`", but the schema accepts the shape and
  `backend/tests/test_validate_uapi.py` validates every golden against it.

## Schema validity of the XML goldens

- Every `*.ubl.xml` and `*.xrechnung.xml` is valid against `UBL-Invoice-2.1.xsd`.
- `it-b2b-sdi`, `it-restaurant-b2c-pec`, `it-restaurant-b2b-fattura`, `it-restaurant-b2g-fpa12` and
  `it-restaurant-td04-credit` are valid against `Schema_VFPR12_v1.2.3.xsd`. `it-restaurant-b2c-pec`
  is the B2C case: `CessionarioCommittente/DatiAnagrafici` carries `CodiceFiscale` with **no**
  `IdFiscaleIVA` (both are `minOccurs="0"` in `DatiAnagraficiCessionarioType`) and `Anagrafica`
  takes the `Nome` + `Cognome` branch of the `xs:choice` in `AnagraficaType` instead of
  `Denominazione`.
- The other `*.fatturapa.xml` files are **negative fixtures**: a Belgian, German or French party
  cannot satisfy the Italian schema (`CAP` is five digits, `Provincia` is two upper-case letters,
  `Telefono` is at most twelve characters). They are kept because they show what a domestic Italian
  schema rejects. `fr-store-b2g-broken.fatturapa.xml` fails for a second, deliberate reason as well:
  with no BT-31 anywhere there is nothing to put in `IdTrasmittente/IdCodice` or in the cedente's
  mandatory `IdFiscaleIVA`. `backend/tests/test_golden_xsd.py` pins the marker for each.
- `*.cii.xml` is **not** covered by `backend/tests/test_golden_xsd.py`: no CII D16B schema is
  vendored, because `tools/fetch_assets.py` has no redistributable pinned source for it and
  `backend/app/validate.py` has no `cii-*` schema key. `formats.ts` therefore sets
  `xsdSchemaKey: null` for the `cii` plugin rather than pointing it at a wrong schema. Both CII
  goldens were checked by hand against the Factur-X 1.08 EN16931 XSD and validate.

## Document references (BT-10 … BT-26) in the fixtures

Every preset carries at least a purchase order (BT-13). The binding used per syntax:

| Business term              | UBL / XRechnung                                                              | CII (Factur-X 1.08 EN16931)                                              | FatturaPA 1.2.3              |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------- |
| BT-10 buyer reference      | `cbc:BuyerReference`                                                         | `ram:ApplicableHeaderTradeAgreement/ram:BuyerReference`                  | —                            |
| BT-11 project reference    | `cac:ProjectReference/cbc:ID`                                                | `ram:SpecifiedProcuringProject/ram:ID` (+ mandatory `ram:Name`)          | —                            |
| BT-12 contract reference   | `cac:ContractDocumentReference/cbc:ID`                                       | `ram:ContractReferencedDocument/ram:IssuerAssignedID`                    | `2.1.3 DatiContratto`        |
| BT-13 purchase order       | `cac:OrderReference/cbc:ID`                                                  | `ram:BuyerOrderReferencedDocument/ram:IssuerAssignedID`                  | `2.1.2 DatiOrdineAcquisto`   |
| BT-14 sales order          | `cac:OrderReference/cbc:SalesOrderID`                                        | `ram:SellerOrderReferencedDocument/ram:IssuerAssignedID`                 | — (no FatturaPA slot)        |
| BT-16 despatch advice      | `cac:DespatchDocumentReference/cbc:ID`                                       | `ram:ApplicableHeaderTradeDelivery/ram:DespatchAdviceReferencedDocument` | `2.1.8 DatiDDT`              |
| BT-17 tender or lot        | `cac:OriginatorDocumentReference/cbc:ID`                                     | `ram:AdditionalReferencedDocument` with `ram:TypeCode` 50                | `2.1.4 DatiConvenzione`      |
| BT-18 invoiced object      | `cac:AdditionalDocumentReference` with `cbc:DocumentTypeCode` 130            | `ram:AdditionalReferencedDocument` with `ram:TypeCode` 130               | `2.1.5 DatiRicezione`        |
| BT-25/26 preceding invoice | `cac:BillingReference/cac:InvoiceDocumentReference/cbc:ID` + `cbc:IssueDate` | `ram:InvoiceReferencedDocument` under `ApplicableHeaderTradeSettlement`  | `2.1.6 DatiFattureCollegate` |

Element order follows the `xsd:sequence` of `InvoiceType` in `UBL-Invoice-2.1.xsd`, of
`HeaderTradeAgreementType` / `HeaderTradeDeliveryType` in the Factur-X 1.08 EN16931 schema and of
`DatiGeneraliType` in `Schema_VFPR12_v1.2.3.xsd`.

Two bindings are approximations and are labelled as such in `fatturapa-map.ts`: FatturaPA has no slot
for BT-14, and BT-18 is carried in `DatiRicezione`, the nearest free `DatiDocumentiCorrelatiType`
block. `DatiDDT` requires both `NumeroDDT` and `DataDDT` (XSD 1.2.3), so the writer emits the block
only when the despatch advice carries a date; BT-16's date is not part of the EN 16931 UBL/CII
bindings and is therefore mapped in FatturaPA only.

## Identifiers in the fixtures are placeholders

Company names, VAT identifiers, codici fiscali, REA numbers, KBO numbers, SIREN/SIRET numbers,
Leitweg-IDs, CIG/CUP codes, IBANs, BICs, SDI destination codes and Peppol participant identifiers in
`src/presets.ts`, together with the purchase order, sales order, contract, convenzione, delivery
note, folio and travel-authorisation references, are **obviously fictitious placeholders**; every e-mail address uses the reserved
`example` name (RFC 2606). At runtime the demo replaces the seller party from `GET /taxpayers/{id}` and
the routing identifiers (`system_id`, `taxpayer_id`, `peppol_id`, buyer destination code) from the
values configured in `.env`; nothing in this directory is used to address a real recipient.

## Schematron findings the goldens are allowed to raise

`tests/schematron-goldens.test.ts` runs every golden through the rule sets a Peppol access point
would apply (`*.ubl.xml` → `cen-ubl` + `peppol-ubl`, `*.xrechnung.xml` → `cen-ubl` +
`xrechnung-ubl`, `*.cii.xml` → `en16931-cii`) and pins the exact set of failing rule ids. A
**native rendering** — a preset serialised in the syntax it declares — must be clean:
`be-peppol.ubl.xml`, `fr-store-b2g-chorus.ubl.xml`, `de-hotel-b2g-xrechnung.xrechnung.xml`,
`de-hotel-b2b-zugferd.cii.xml`, `fr-store-b2b-facturx.cii.xml`. `be-peppol-broken.ubl.xml` is the
one native rendering that cannot be clean — the preset exists to fail a Peppol rule and Belgium's
own syntax is UBL — so that test needs a deliberately-broken exemption alongside its expectations.

Cross-format renderings keep the findings that follow from the scenario, not from a defect:

- `PEPPOL-EN16931-CL008` on `de-hotel-b2b-zugferd.ubl.xml` (×2) and
  `de-hotel-b2g-xrechnung.ubl.xml` (×1) — EAS `EM` is a CEF code and correct for an EN 16931
  invoice delivered by e-mail, but is not in the Peppol EAS subset.
- `PEPPOL-EN16931-R010` on `it-restaurant-b2g-fpa12.ubl.xml` — the ministry is addressed by its
  codice univoco ufficio over SDI, so the Peppol rendering has no BT-49.
- `BR-CL-01` + `PEPPOL-EN16931-P0100` on `it-restaurant-td04-credit.ubl.xml` — a credit note in an
  Invoice document, which `formats.ts` refuses to offer in the app.
- `PEPPOL-EN16931-R003` + `PEPPOL-EN16931-R010` on `it-restaurant-b2c-pec.ubl.xml` — a private
  guest places no purchase order and has no buyer reference, and she is reached over SDI by PEC
  rather than by a Peppol participant id. An Italian B2C invoice is not a Peppol document; giving
  it a BT-10 or a BT-49 would invent both.

One finding is an **engine defect, not a data defect**: `BR-DE-19` (XRechnung) and `DE-R-019`
(Peppol) rebuild BT-84 into the 24-digit ISO 13616 number and take it `mod 97`. SaxonJS 2.7 — the
newest release — stores `xs:integer` exactly but evaluates `mod` in IEEE-754 doubles, so
`DE89370400440532013000` (a valid IBAN: `xs:decimal(…) mod 97` = 1, and `presets.test.ts` checks
every preset IBAN with BigInt) is reported as invalid. Saxon-HE and the official KoSIT validator
accept it. Do not swap the IBAN for one whose rounded value happens to land on 1.

## Deliberate defects

Four presets — one per country — exist to fail, and each fails on something characteristic of that
country's format, so the Validate step teaches a different lesson in each row of the matrix.

### `broken` (IT, FatturaPA) — the model stage

1. `BR-CO-14` — BT-110 (`210.00`) does not equal the sum of the VAT breakdown (`220.00`).
2. `BR-11` — the buyer postal address has no country code.
3. `BR-E-10` — the exempt (`E` / Natura `N4`) breakdown row has neither BT-120 nor BT-121.
4. `CHANNEL-SDI-PEC` — destination code `0000000` without a PEC address.

All four are business-rule defects, not schema defects, so `broken.ubl.xml` still satisfies the UBL
2.1 XSD; `broken.fatturapa.xml` does not, because the missing country code leaves `Sede` without the
mandatory `Nazione`.

### `de-hotel-b2g-broken` (DE, XRechnung 3.0.2) — the CIUS additions

BT-10 carries no Leitweg-ID and the seller has no BT-42 telephone number. Both are optional in
EN 16931 and mandatory in the German CIUS, so the model stage and the XSD stage stay clean and only
Schematron fires: `BR-DE-15` (fatal), `BR-DE-6` (fatal) and `BR-DE-27` (warning, the follow-on rule
asking BT-42 for at least three digits) in `xrechnung-ubl`. The same defects surface in the
cross-format `de-hotel-b2g-broken.ubl.xml` as the Peppol national rules `DE-R-015`, `DE-R-006` and
`DE-R-027`.

### `be-peppol-broken` (BE, Peppol BIS Billing 3.0) — the KBO check digit

The buyer's Belgian enterprise number is `0888888896`. `PEPPOL-COMMON-R043` runs the mod-97 rule
over every ICD 0208 identifier — the last two digits must equal `97 - (the first eight mod 97)`,
which is `95` — so the endpoint (BT-49) and the legal registration identifier (BT-47) each raise it,
twice in total. Nothing else in the invoice changes, and the model stage stays clean because the
Peppol participant id is still syntactically well formed.

### `fr-store-b2g-broken` (FR, Factur-X 1.08 CII for Chorus Pro) — SIRET instead of TVA

The seller files its SIRET in BT-30 (ISO 6523 scheme `0002`) and no numéro de TVA
intracommunautaire in BT-31, while every line charges the 20% standard rate: `BR-S-02` (fatal, once
per line). `BR-CO-26` is still satisfied by BT-30, which is exactly why the model stage cannot see
this and the CEN rule set can. BT-10 has also lost the _code service_ Chorus Pro routes on — a
platform rejection that no EN 16931 rule in this app can detect, which is the second half of the
lesson.
